transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t stop thinking something’s wrong with my face. Mostly the left side. In photos, or on my online class camera, my nose and jaw look crooked to me.

People say they don’t notice it, but I still feel like everyone in the CNC lab sees that first, before anything I’m doing.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors or adjusting your face, because of concerns about how you look?

Yeah… I do. Mostly before I leave for school. I’ll get stuck in the bathroom mirror, then check my phone camera too. I keep fixing my hair or changing shirts, trying to make my face look less… angled, I guess.

Sometimes I ask my mom if it looks weird. It can take a long time. I’ve missed lab before, or I get there and I’m already too drained to really focus.
Do you believe that your facial asymmetry makes you look unattractive or deformed?

Yeah… I do. I know people say they don’t see it, but to me the left side looks wrong. Like my nose and jaw are crooked, especially in ID photos or on camera.

It’s hard not to feel like it makes me look… messed up, I guess. And then I think everyone in the lab notices that before anything else.
Do you think your concern about your face is something that most people wouldn't notice, or do you believe others see it as clearly as you do?

I mean… people tell me they don’t really see it. So maybe most people wouldn’t notice it the way I do.

But it doesn’t feel that way. When I’m in class or in the CNC lab, I feel like they can see the left side of my face is off—like my nose and jaw look crooked—and that’s the first thing they notice.
How much time would you say you spend most days thinking about your face or checking how it looks?

Most days… a lot. I don’t really know the exact number, but it feels like it’s in the back of my head almost all day.

I keep thinking the left side of my face looks off, like my nose and jaw are crooked. Especially if I see myself in an ID photo or on the online class camera. Even when people say they don’t notice it, I still feel like everyone in the CNC lab sees that before anything else.
Have you noticed these concerns about your face getting worse during times when you're feeling more down or depressed?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid attention to whether it’s tied to that exactly.

I mean, when I feel worse in general, I probably think about it more… but I don’t know if it actually gets worse or if I just notice it more.
Do these thoughts about your face ever get so intense that they interfere with your ability to focus on schoolwork, interact with others, or participate in activities you usually do?

Yeah… it does.

I’ve missed some CNC labs and shop shifts because I just couldn’t make myself leave. I’d get ready and then keep thinking about my face, and… I just wouldn’t go.

My faculty mentor said my work placement could be in trouble if it keeps happening. And I stopped playing soccer and volunteering, mostly because I don’t want people looking at me.

Do you find yourself doing certain things over and over again, like checking your face in the mirror, taking multiple photos, or adjusting your clothes, because you’re worried about how your face looks?

Yeah… I do.

Before school I’ll get stuck in the bathroom mirror, then checking my phone camera too. I’ll keep fixing my hair or changing shirts because I think it makes the angle look less bad.

Sometimes I ask my mom if it looks weird… even though I don’t really want to ask. And it can go on long enough that I miss lab, or I get there and I’m already too drained to focus.
When you feel anxious or stuck about your face, does it come with a low mood, loss of interest in things, or feelings of worthlessness, or does it mostly stay focused on how you look?

It mostly stays on how I look, I think.

Like… I came in because I can’t stop thinking the left side of my face looks off. My nose, my jaw… in ID photos or on the online class camera, it just looks crooked to me. Even when people say they don’t notice it, I still feel like everyone in the CNC lab sees that before they see anything I’m doing.
Do you feel that your concern about your face is excessive, even if you can't stop thinking about it?

Yeah… I mean, part of me knows it probably sounds excessive.

But when I see my face in an ID photo or on the online class camera, the left side just looks wrong to me—like my nose and jaw are crooked. People say they don’t see it, but I still feel like everyone in the CNC lab notices that before anything else.
